match.reason: The closest bank card, eco-australia-exports-imports, is a Year 12 profile of Australia's specific trade mix with questions on fuel imports, which is deeper and broader than the Year 9 definition this point needs, and the other two cards cover government spending and aggregate demand.

draft.title: Exports and imports
card: a good or service sold to buyers in another country. The money comes into the seller's country.
a good or service bought from sellers in another country. The money goes out to the foreign seller.

Services count too, not only goods. A tourist from abroad who stays at a hotel in Cairns is buying an export. An Australian who pays a foreign company for a streaming subscription is buying an import.
The same item is an export for one country and an import for another. Ask who is selling and who is buying: the seller's country exports, and the buyer's country imports.
draft.remember: Exports are sold out to other countries. Imports are bought in from them.

a.q: A winery in the Barossa Valley sells wine to a shop in Singapore. What is this sale for Australia?
opts: An export
An import
A domestic sale
A service import
a.why: The wine is sold by an Australian business to a buyer in another country, so it is an export for Australia. It is not an import, because Australia is the seller, not the buyer.
a.clue: Is Australia the seller or the buyer here?

b.q: Priya, who lives in Perth, pays a software company in Ireland for a design app. Another student, Tom, visits Perth from Japan and pays for a tour. Which pair is correct for Australia?
opts: Priya's payment is an import, Tom's tour is an export
Priya's payment is an export, Tom's tour is an import
Both are imports, as money crosses the border each time
Both are exports, as both are services and not goods
b.why: Priya buys from a foreign seller, so for Australia it is an import, even though it is a service. Tom is a foreign buyer of an Australian service, so it is an export. Which way the money moves, not whether it is a good or service, decides the label.
b.clue: Check who is buying in each case, and where they live.

b.best: Priya's payment is an import, Tom's tour is an export

problems.detail: The stem calls Tom 'another student', but Priya is never described as a student. This is a small inconsistency that could briefly confuse a reader. It does not change the answer.
